notes: Anchored corpus for PolyDiff opengraph-family rediscovery + synthetic regressions.
Witnesses are pinned by SHA-256 ONLY. NO payload bytes appear in this repo.

Anchors cover four canonical opengraph divergence shapes: og_url (MEDIUM-HIGH; FB crawler relative-URL class), twitter_card_type/twitter_image (MEDIUM; player XSS class), oembed canonical_url (MEDIUM; provider-origin-confusion), decode_outcome (HIGH; synthetic meta tag quote-escape parser crash).
Per-case `implementations` lists the two wrapper ids the case is designed to disagree on; the diff engine runs ALL declared wrappers and picks up these axes (plus any others that surface).
Per-case `expected_fact_vector_diff` is keyed by axis name; each value is a 2-element array of the two impls' observations (matches the `implementations` ordering).

cases.summary: Facebook crawler resolved relative URLs (e.g. './landing') against the crawled page's URL differently from WHATWG-URL conformant downstream consumers (~2018). One side resolved to attacker-controlled origin; the other to victim. Public link-preview bypass class.
cases.reference_url: https://www.facebook.com/business/help/docs (historical OG crawler documentation; specific 2018 bug write-up archived under engineering-private).
cases.limitations: witness bytes are NOT in this repo; pinned-hash anchor only. The expected fact-vector diff documents the canonical disagreement shape — actual parser outputs depend on the pinned wrapper versions.

cases.summary: Twitter Card `player` type had inconsistent URL sanitization between Twitter's crawler and downstream embedders. One impl emitted a player URL with un-sanitized javascript:-scheme prefix; the other rejected it as not-a-card. Historical XSS-prone link preview class.
cases.limitations: twitter:player URL field is the historical sanitization-divergence vector; we surface it via twitter_card_type divergence in the public fact-vector axes (the URL itself is treated as an opaque string per the schema).

cases.summary: When OG metadata and the oEmbed provider JSON response declare DIFFERENT canonical URLs for the same page, downstream consumers picked inconsistently — the attacker-controlled OG URL or the legit oEmbed URL — based on parser priority. The attacker controlled whichever one the downstream trusted.
cases.limitations: synthetic case constructed to exercise the canonical_url divergence triage rule. The oEmbed response payload and the OG HTML are supplied as separate witness bytes in private corpus (each wrapper sees only its own payload).

cases.summary: Synthetic anchor: <meta name='og:title' content='he said "hi"'> uses nested quote chars. One impl crashes the underlying HTML tokenizer; another truncates the title at the first inner quote; a third returns the full string. Exercises decode_outcome divergence (HIGH triage).
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design constructed to exercise the decode_outcome divergence triage rule
